C-44, ss. 21.1-21.4, 23.1 and applicable regulations, as amended by the Federal Beneficial Ownership Transparency Act (Budget Implementation Act, 2023, No. 1, S.C. 2023, c. 26); FINTRAC compliance program and record-keeping obligations under the PCMLTFA and corresponding regulations; Corporations Canada beneficial ownership registry directives.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Passport Authority / National Civil Registry of the UBO's country of origin
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille Convention (or Consular Legalization if the origin country is not an Apostille member)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified banker's reference letter confirming the UBO's identity and funding source, addressed to the proposed corporate service provider
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Bank or recognized financial institution in the UBO's jurisdiction of residence
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or Consular Legalization if the institution requires external documentary legalization; otherwise institutional stamp and officer attestation

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized UBO declaration and ownership structure chart, including ultimate beneficial owner particulars
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary Public in the UBO's jurisdiction or the corporate service provider's local notary, as applicable
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille in the jurisdiction where the notary is commissioned (or Consular Legalization for non-Hague states)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified certificate of incumbency, certificate of good standing, or articles of incorporation for each entity in the upstream ownership chain
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent companies registry or corporate secretary in each upstream entity's jurisdiction

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory enhanced customer due diligence under FINTRAC guidance for M&A advisory services categorized as Medium_Risk_Enhanced. All confirmed and ultimate beneficial owners, directors, officers, and authorized signatories must be screened against: Canadian sanctions lists administered under the Special Economic Measures Act, S.C. 1992, c. 17; the United Nations Act, S.C. 1991, c. 49; the Freeze Asset provisions under PCMLTFA; OFAC Specially Designated Nationals and Blocked Persons List; UN Security Council Consolidated List; domestic Canadian law enforcement watchlists; and Politically Exposed Persons (domestic and foreign) databases. Independent third-party AML screening software is required with audit-trail retention for five years after termination of business relationship.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Corporations Canada Online Filing Centre (corporate name search and reservation through the Canadian corporate registry system, NUANS)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Corporate names must be in English or French, or a transliterated version of either; the name must include a legal element such as Inc., Corp., Ltd., Incorporated, Limitée, Société par actions de régime fédéral, or an approved abbreviation. The proposed name must not be confusingly similar to an existing federal or provincial corporate name, trademark, or other protected mark. Distinctive word or phrase, descriptive element, and legal element are required; foreign names must be adequately transliterated into the Roman alphabet or French/English characters for the NUANS search.

stage_1.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon name rejection, the applicant or authorized agent must obtain the written rejection reasons from Corporations Canada, prepare a written submission addressing the confusing similarity grounds and any prohibited token concerns, and file a notice of appeal or reconsideration via the Corporations Canada contact portal within 30 days of rejection. Where the Director's reconsideration is refused, the applicant may seek judicial review in the Federal Court of Canada under the Federal Courts Act, R.S.C. 1985, c. F-7, or may file a revised NUANS search and repeated reservation request with a new distinctive element. Appeal should be supported by a statutory declaration, trademark coexistence or consent letters where applicable, and evidence of non-confusion.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Permitted only if the virtual office provider maintains a physical street address in the declared province and provides for receipt of legal process and director records; the registered office cannot be a post office box. For an M&A advisory boutique, a virtual office generally satisfies CBCA formalities but is commercially disfavored by financial counterparties and FINTRAC examiners unless the provider offers physical meeting space and bank account reception.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Moderate risk, estimated at 20-30% within the first three operating years, driven by corporate services industry triggers, registered office consistency checks, and FINTRAC compliance examinations applicable to M&A intermediaries.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Canada Business Corporations Act, R.S.C. 1985, c. C-44, as amended (sections 8, 9, 16, 25, 101, 106, 109, 113, 114 and 266)
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Corporations Canada, Innovation, Science and Economic Development Canada (ISED)
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Articles of Incorporation (Form 1) under the Canada Business Corporations Act
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital; no escrow deposit or capital holdback required under the CBCA; shares may be issued for such consideration as the directors determine pursuant to section 25
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, that the Corporation subscribes for, accepts, and issues to each proposed director named in the Notice of Directors one common share for organizational purposes; AND RESOLVED, that the registered office of the Corporation shall be located at [Street Address], [City], [Province], and that the required Notice of Registered Office and Notice of Directors be filed promptly with Corporations Canada; AND RESOLVED, that [Name] be appointed Chief Executive Officer, [Name] be appointed Chief Financial Officer, and [Name] be appointed Corporate Secretary, each to serve at the pleasure of the Board; AND RESOLVED, that management is authorized to open corporate bank accounts, adopt bylaws, and execute all ancillary instruments.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Conduct Federal Name Search and Reservation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: NUANS via Corporations Canada online portal (CRS system)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit a proposed corporate name through the Corporations Canada online filing portal; obtain an automated NUANS name search report verifying distinctiveness; reserve the approved name for a 90-day period or incorporate using a numbered name (e.g., 12345678 Canada Inc.).
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is rejected as confusing or nondistinctive, file a revised name search request with alternative names or adopt the assigned numbered name and subsequently apply for a name change by Articles of Amendment.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Draft and File Articles of Incorporation (Form 1)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Corporations Canada – online incorporation filing window
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Complete Form 1 specifying corporate name, province of registered office, share structure (including any rights, privileges, restrictions, and conditions), number and minimum/maximum directors, and any restrictions on share transfers or business activities; submit electronically via the CRS portal and pay the statutory filing fee by credit card.
required_dossiers: NUANS name search report or numbered name designation
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If a deficiency letter is issued by Corporations Canada, respond within 30 days through the CRS portal by amending the affected clauses; otherwise the application is deemed abandoned and the fee forfeited.

step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Upon approval, download the electronic Certificate of Incorporation from the CRS portal; verify the corporation name, date of incorporation, corporation number, and jurisdiction; retain the certificate as conclusive evidence of incorporation under section 9 CBCA.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If any clerical typographical error appears in the certificate or articles, apply under section 266 CBCA to the Director for a correction of the certificate.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: File Initial Registered Office and Notice of Directors (Form 2)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Within 15 days after incorporation, file Form 2 stating the street address of the registered office (which must be within the province named in the articles) and the names, residential addresses, and consent status of all first directors; the directors must be natural persons who are not bankrupt and, if not resident Canadians, must be within the permitted director residency thresholds.
required_dossiers: Initial Registered Office and Notice of Directors (Form 2)
Consent to act as director forms
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the filing is rejected for incomplete director information, correct and refile immediately; late filings after 15 days are not a criminal default but expose the corporation to dissolution or administrative penalties, which are cured by an updated Form 2/3 filing.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Register Federal Business Number with CRA
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) – Business Registration Online (BRO)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Register with the CRA to obtain a federal Business Number (BN), a Corporation Income Tax account, a GST/HST account, and, if employees will be hired, a Payroll Deductions account; capitalize the corporation under the CBCA and file the initial corporate notice of assessment under the Income Tax Act.
required_dossiers: CRA Business Registration Online application data
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If CRA registration is delayed or queried, contact the CRA Business Enquiries line to reconcile the BN, or file a written explanation with the local tax services office; all accounts are interlinked to the BN.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Adopt Bylaws, Issue Shares, and Open Bank Account
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Corporations Canada (bylaw recordation) / corporate directors and officers (governance)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: At the first board meeting or by unanimous written resolution, adopt Bylaw No. 1 containing governance procedures, issue share certificates to the subscribers and directors, appoint officers, approve banking resolutions, and execute the corporate minute book and securities register accordingly.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If a procedural defect is later identified, the shareholders may ratify the act by ordinary resolution, or the directors may rescind and reissue the instrument to ensure compliance with the CBCA.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Canadian Securities Administrators (CSA) acting through the provincial securities commission of the province where the M&A advisory boutique holds its principal office; supplemented by the Canadian Investment Regulatory Organization (CIRO) for dealer-manager oversight
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Exempt Market Dealer Registration under National Instrument 31-103, or Limited Dealer/M&A Advisor exemption where applicable; FINTRAC registration as a reporting entity for large transaction and wire transfer compliance

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Impact Assessment Agency of Canada (federal), with provincial municipal environmental coordination
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt – Class Screening Exclusion for commercial office and professional advisory operations (non-physical, non-manufacturing activity)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No industrial wastewater discharge; office HVAC VOC emissions within Canadian Ambient Air Quality Standards; electronic waste disposal per provincial E-waste Regulation; general waste handled under municipal commercial waste management bylaws

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety inspection and occupancy permit under the National Fire Code of Canada issued by municipal fire marshal; structural load certification for professional office occupancy per the National Building Code; provincial/territorial occupational health and safety clearance (Workers' Compensation Board coverage) for employees of the advisory firm

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) / Agence du revenu du Canada (ARC). Primary portals: Business Registration Online (BRO), CRA My Business Account, GST/HST NETFILE, and the CARM customs client portal. Provincial tax administration is separate; Revenu Québec administers the QST, while the CRA administers GST/HST and corporate income tax in all other provinces.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Step 1: Incorporate federally under the Canada Business Corporations Act or register an extra-provincial presence; the CRA assigns a 9-digit Business Number (BN), which is the sole statutory federal tax identifier. Step 2: Apply for the BN and program accounts via Business Registration Online, by mail/fax on Form RC1 (Request for a Business Number), or through the integrated provincial registry; a non-resident applicant must provide a Canadian address for service and may appoint a Canadian representative. Step 3: The CRA activates the RP (corporate income tax) and RT (GST/HST) program accounts automatically or upon application; RC (payroll), RM (customs), and RD (information returns) accounts are added when applicable. Step 4: A foreign corporation carrying on business in Canada must register for GST/HST before making taxable supplies once the CAD 30,000 small-supplier threshold is exceeded; a non-resident making only zero-rated supplies may register voluntarily to claim input tax credits. Online BN issuance typically takes 2–5 business days; the BN confirmation notice is the statutory tax identification document.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation. A Canadian business corporation is a separate taxpayer subject to Part I of the Income Tax Act on worldwide income if resident; a non-resident-owned corporation is taxed only on Canadian-source income (including business income and taxable Canadian property gains). The corporation is not pass-through eligible and, if foreign-controlled, is denied the small business deduction; the federal general corporate rate is 15% (provincial corporate income tax is levied separately). Dividends paid to non-resident shareholders bear Part XIII withholding (25% statutory, treaty-reduced to 5–15%).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Canada has no US-style check-the-box classification election. Available statutory elections for a foreign-controlled M&A boutique include: (i) ITA s. 85(1) rollover election on qualifying asset transfers to/from a corporation; (ii) ITA ss. 87 and 88.1 elections on amalgamations and wind-ups; (iii) Excise Tax Act ss. 156, 167, and 273 elections to eliminate GST/HST on supplies between closely related registrants; (iv) an election to treat a supply as a financial service under Schedule V, Part VII of the Excise Tax Act; and (v) OECD hybrid-mismatch response rules (effective 1 July 2022) that contain limited timing elections but no entity-level check-the-box.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Canada (Banque du Canada) as monetary authority; Office of the Superintendent of Financial Institutions (OSFI) as prudential bank regulator; Financial Transactions and Reports Analysis Centre of Canada (FINTRAC) as AML/ATF supervisory body; Statistics Canada as balance-of-payments reporter for cross-border capital transactions
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The Canadian dollar (CAD) is fully convertible on both current and capital accounts. Canada operates a purely floating exchange rate regime since May 1970 with no exchange control legislation in force; the former Foreign Exchange Control Board regime was repealed, and neither the Currency Act (RSC 1985, c C-52) nor the Bank of Canada Act (RSC 1985, c B-2) imposes restrictions on capital inflows, outflows, dividend remittances, or profit repatriation. An M&A advisory boutique may receive success fees and retainers from foreign counterparties and repatriate funds to non-resident shareholders without prior Bank of Canada or OSFI approval. The sole fiscal constraint is Part XIII non-resident withholding tax under the Income Tax Act (Canada) (RSC 1985, c 1, 5th Supp), generally 25% statutory, reduced by applicable tax treaty (e.g., 5% to 15% under the Canada-US treaty), payable on dividends, interest, royalties, and certain management or advisory fees sourced to Canada. The Investment Canada Act (RSC 1985, c 28, 1st Supp) review thresholds apply only to an acquisition of control of a Canadian business (2024 WTO threshold: C$1.335 billion) and do not impede ordinary capital injection routing for a boutique advisory entity.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: No statutory surrender, conversion, or repatriation obligation exists under any Canadian federal statute. Canada imposes zero mandatory exchange-surrender ratios, zero minimum conversion period, and zero CAD conversion requirement for export proceeds or cross-border service fees. Receipts from cross-border M&A advisory services may be retained in any permitted currency. The only applicable requirements are AML/reporting obligations under the Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act (SC 2000, c 17) and its regulations (SOR/2002-184), including reporting of all incoming and outgoing international electronic fund transfers of C$10,000 or more to FINTRAC, and statistical classification of transactions in Statistics Canada surveys; neither triggers a surrender duty.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating: LOW for primary treasury and escrow functions; MEDIUM as supplemental payment-access conduit. Under the Bank Act (SC 1991, c 46), only Schedule I or Schedule II chartered banks and authorized foreign bank branches may accept deposits in Canada as a banking business; offshore digital EMIs (e.g., Wise, Payoneer, Airwallex) are not authorized deposit-taking institutions under Canadian law. Such providers may operate as money service businesses (MSBs) or foreign money service businesses (FMSBs) registered with FINTRAC, enabling sub-account foreign-currency collection and low-value vendor payments, but they cannot lawfully provide statutory escrow, commercial letters of credit, investment-grade settlement, or CAD Lynx high-value clearing. A federally incorporated M&A boutique must therefore maintain its primary settlement relationship with a Schedule I bank; EMI rails are permissible only for ancillary disbursements and must be linked to a compliant Schedule I master account to avoid PCMLTFA contraventions if unregistered services are used.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Remote opening is legally permitted: PCMLTF Regulations (SOR/2002-184, ss 59-62) allow identity verification via notarized certified copies, electronic verification methods, legal-counsel referrals, and credit-file verification, without any absolute statutory in-person appearance. In practice, however, all major Canadian Schedule I banks require at least one of the following: (i) an in-person KYC interview at a Canadian branch for the director or authorized signatory; (ii) a notarized identity package executed before a Canadian consular official abroad and couriered to the opening branch; or (iii) an existing correspondent-client referral from a foreign qualifying bank. For non-resident-owned holding structures, banks will generally mandate physical presence of at least one director (or completion of a bank-approved video-trust-identity procedure) and will subject the account to enhanced due diligence with a 30-to-60-business-day review window. The recommended path for this boutique is an in-person opening at the RBC or TD international banking centre in Toronto with the principal director, supported by a Canadian corporate counsel covering letter.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident directors or shareholders controlling greater than 25% of the CBCA corporation, particularly through an offshore intermediate holding company
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Complete organizational chart tracing ultimate beneficial ownership; Corporations Canada certified articles and annual return; notarized shareholder register and share-transfer ledger; source-of-wealth statement for each ultimate beneficial owner; tax residency certificates from the owner's jurisdiction; written AML narrative explaining the cross-border M&A advisory revenue model and counterparty jurisdictions.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Success-fee and retainer flows from foreign private companies and trusts in the deal pipeline, creating source-of-funds ambiguity
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Signed engagement letters with defined success-fee milestones; itemized invoices matching deliverables; underlying sale-purchase agreements evidencing bona fide advisory work; audited or accountant-reviewed financial statements; bank reference letters from the client's remitting institution; FINTRAC-compliant records of large-value transaction origins.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Client geography overlapped by sanctions programs (e.g., adversarial jurisdictions referenced in Special Economic Measures Act (SC 1992, c 17) or United Nations Act (RSC 1985, c U-2) schedules)
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Written sanctions-screening policy; proof of daily screening of clients, beneficial owners, and counterparties against OSFI and Global Affairs Canada sanctioned-party lists; transaction-level risk-rating memos; enhanced due diligence files on any jurisdiction-adjacent counterparty; board-approved statement confirming no dealings with sanctioned persons or entities.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Politically Exposed Persons (PEP) or head-of-international-organization status of a director, shareholder, or advisory principal
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Signed PEP declarations for all directors and beneficial owners; independent commercial PEP database screening reports; personal net-worth and source-of-funds attestations; two professional reference letters from regulated financial or legal advisors; compliance-officer sign-off memorandum documenting enhanced transaction monitoring.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Compliant routing for non-resident parent equity injection into the federally incorporated boutique: remit via SWIFT MT103 from the parent's bank to the beneficiary account at a Canadian Schedule I bank using the bank's BIC (e.g., ROYCCAT2 for RBC, TDOMCATTTOR for TD, NOSCCATT for Scotiabank) and the 15-digit Canadian clearing code (5-digit transit + 3-digit institution + 7-digit account). The MT103 field 70 (Remittance Information) must state 'Capital Injection – Direct Investment under CBCA' and reference the corporate resolution; field 50K must identify the ordering non-resident entity. The payment purpose must align with the Statistics Canada Nature of Payment classification for direct investment and capital transfers (capital account category, not current account revenues). For USD-denominated injections, the funds convert to CAD at the bank's prevailing corporate rate; receiving bank may require the shareholder resolution, proceedings, and beneficial ownership declaration prior to crediting. All inbound transfers above C$10,000 are reportable to FINTRAC as international electronic fund transfers; the bank will require the corporate files used in onboarding to remain current for verification.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Primary clearing rails: (1) SWIFT MT103 for retainer payments, cross-border success fees, advisor co-payments, and operating disbursements, with beneficiary identification in field 57A and settlement purpose in field 70; (2) Commercial Letters of Credit (documentary credit per UCP 600) for cross-border deal-related milestone payments or escrowed working-capital settlements, issued by the Canadian Schedule I bank at the boutique's request; (3) SWIFT MT202 COV for interbank cover payments routed through correspondent banks; (4) Payments Canada Lynx for high-value CAD settlements exceeding C$25 million per day; (5) Payments Canada Real-Time Rail for instant sub-C$100,000 disbursements. Each outbound payment must reference the underlying engagement agreement or invoice to support the AML/ATF review and must clear sanctions screening under the Special Economic Measures Act and United Nations Act; payments to sanctioned jurisdictions or parties are prohibited and may constitute criminal violations.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Vanilla FX Forwards: outright CAD/USD and CAD/EUR forward contracts with maturities up to 24 months, documented under a bank-standard ISDA Master Agreement with FX Annex or a standalone forward confirmation; permitted without exchange-control approval
FX Swaps: simultaneous spot and forward legs for CAD/USD liquidity management on advisory-fee cash flows
Cross-Currency Swaps: CAD/USD EUR/USD interest-rate-and-principal exchange structures under the ISDA 2002 Master Agreement, permissible for hedging balance-sheet and deferred-fee exposures
European-Style Currency Options: plain-vanilla CAD/USD calls and puts purchased for protection against adverse conversion on large success-fee receipts; premium payable in CAD or USD

Non-Deliverable Forwards (NDFs): legally permissible and unregulated as to availability, but practically unnecessary because CAD is a fully convertible and deliverable currency; NDFs are not restricted by any Canadian statute but would carry onshore-offshore basis risk and are not recommended for this treasury profile

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Federal Annual Return under CBCA s.133
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Corporations Canada, Innovation, Science and Economic Development Canada
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 60 days after each incorporation anniversary
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing fee of CAD 200 (approx. USD 148); dissolution proceedings may be initiated by Director after two consecutive years of default

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: T2 Federal Corporation Income Tax Return
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Penalty of 5% of unpaid tax plus 1% per month up to 12 months; directors may be liable for unremitted corporate tax

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: One month after fiscal year-end for annual filers; monthly/quarterly based on revenue
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Penalty of 5% of unpaid amount plus 1% per month; interest at prescribed rates; possible set-off against refunds

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: No revenue-based threshold; mandatory audit for distributing corporations; non-distributing corporations may opt out by unanimous shareholder agreement
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: IFRS for public enterprises; Canadian ASPE for private corporations

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: No beneficial ownership filing with annual return; maintain a register of individuals with significant control internally and update within 15 days of any major shareholding or control change
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Individuals with Significant Control

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 15% federal general corporate income tax rate under Part I after General Rate Reduction; provincial corporate tax rates of 8%–16% apply in addition for a combined headline rate of approximately 23%–31% depending on province and permanent establishment allocation.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Canadian-Controlled Private Corporation (CCPC) Small Business Deduction: federal 9% effective rate on the first CAD 500,000 of active business income; General Rate Reduction of 13% (federal 15% general rate); Scientific Research and Experimental Development (SR&ED) refundable investment tax credits up to 35% (CCPC) or 15% (non-CCPC); foreign tax credit on foreign-source income; intercorporate dividend exemption (typically 0% tax on taxable dividends received); provincial innovation/manufacturing credits potentially available.
